# Validating scenarios (Rust)

A scenario's `up`/`down` is ordinary code, but its `down` is easy to get subtly wrong, so validate every scenario against a real database before it reaches production.

There is **no `check_scenario` helper** in the Rust SDK. You validate by driving the same entry point the platform hits - `handle_request(&config, &req).await` - through a full `up` then `down` cycle in a `#[tokio::test]`, signing each request body with `hmac::sign_body`. That runs your real `up`/`down` and the teardown-token round-trip exactly as production would. No HTTP server required.

## The cycle in one test

Build the same `HandlerConfig` you mount in production (so the secrets and signing behavior match), then send a signed `up`, pull the `teardownToken` out of the response, and send it back as a signed `down`. Assert the status codes.

```rust
// tests/validate_scenarios.rs
use std::collections::HashMap;

use autonoma_sdk::handler::handle_request;
use autonoma_sdk::hmac::sign_body;
use autonoma_sdk::types::{HandlerConfig, HandlerRequest};
use serde_json::{json, Value};

const SHARED: &str = "check-shared-secret";
const SIGNING: &str = "check-signing-secret"; // must differ from SHARED

fn signed_request(body: &str) -> HandlerRequest {
    let mut headers = HashMap::new();
    headers.insert("x-signature".to_string(), sign_body(body, SHARED));
    HandlerRequest { body: body.to_string(), headers }
}

fn config() -> HandlerConfig {
    // Point your DB client at a real (test) database here, then build the
    // exact same config your production handler uses.
    #[allow(deprecated)]
    HandlerConfig {
        shared_secret: SHARED.to_string(),
        signing_secret: SIGNING.to_string(),
        scenarios: my_app::scenarios::scenarios(),
        expires_in_seconds: None,
        allow_production: false,
        sdk: None,
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn single_user_up_then_down() {
    let config = config();

    // up
    let up_body = json!({
        "action": "up",
        "scenario": { "name": "single-user" },
        "testRunId": "check-run-1"
    })
    .to_string();
    let up = handle_request(&config, &signed_request(&up_body)).await;
    assert_eq!(up.status, 200, "up failed: {}", up.body);

    // down: feed the teardownToken from up straight back
    let token = up.body["teardownToken"].as_str().expect("teardownToken");
    let down_body = json!({
        "action": "down",
        "teardownToken": token,
        "testRunId": "check-run-1"
    })
    .to_string();
    let down = handle_request(&config, &signed_request(&down_body)).await;
    assert_eq!(down.status, 200, "down failed: {}", down.body);
    assert_eq!(down.body["ok"], Value::Bool(true));
}
```

Run it with `cargo test`. Loop over `config().scenarios` (calling `.name()` on each) to validate your whole registry in one test if you prefer.

## Reading the result

`handle_request` never panics on a scenario failure - it returns a `HandlerResponse { status, body }`. A `200` means the action succeeded; anything else carries an error body `{ "error": ..., "code": ... }`.

| You see | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| `up.status == 200` | Provisioning succeeded. |
| `up.status == 500`, `code == "INTERNAL_ERROR"` (or the scenario's own `AutonomaError`) | `up` returned an `Err` - provisioning code threw before returning. |
| `down.status == 200`, `ok == true` | Teardown succeeded (or the scenario defines no `down`, which is a no-op). |
| `down.status == 403`, `code == "INVALID_TEARDOWN_TOKEN"` | The teardown token did not verify - almost always different secrets between the `up` config and the `down` config. Use one config for both. |

## The fix loop

Validation is iterative, especially the first time you write a scenario:

1. Run the test.
2. If a status is not `200`, read `resp.body["error"]` and `resp.body["code"]`.
3. Fix the scenario code and re-run.
4. Repeat until both `up` and `down` return `200`.

Common failures and fixes:

| Message / code | Cause | Fix |
|----------------|-------|-----|
| `Unique constraint ... email` (in the `up` error) | A unique value was not seeded from `test_run_id`, so two runs collide | Derive it with `unique_email` / `unique_slug` / `unique_id` from `ctx.test_run_id`. |
| An error at `down` (`status != 200`) | `down` referenced a handle `up` never put in `teardown`, or deleted in the wrong order | Return every id `down` needs from `up` as `teardown`, and delete children before parents. |
| `up` returned `INTERNAL_ERROR` before responding | Provisioning code failed (missing required field, bad FK) | Fix the creation call; run the same code path your app uses in production. |
| `INVALID_TEARDOWN_TOKEN` on `down` | `up` and `down` used different `signing_secret`s | Build one `HandlerConfig` and reuse it for both halves of the cycle. |

Point your DB client at a throwaway database for these tests - a local test Postgres, a testcontainers instance, or an ephemeral schema - because `up`/`down` run your real writes and deletes.
